title: Partner badge eligibility and pricing bundle edge cases
body:
Purpose: quick working reference for badge eligibility rules + pricing bundle design decisions, focusing on unusual scenarios that have tripped launches before. This is a lightweight playbook for GTM, legal, and platform to align on acceptance criteria and mitigations

Quick summary:
- Primary goal: define deterministic gate rules for awarding a marketplace partner "Redwood Verified" badge and ensure pricing bundles behave predictably across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.
- This doc collects edge-case scenarios (trial entitlements, dual-SKU products, reseller markup, metered vs subscription billing) + proposed guardrails and sample copy snippets for listing content.
- Status: draft. Intended to inform the RMKT-3421 epic and feed into the listing preflight checklist.

1) Badge eligibility (high-level rules)
- Core requirements (must be true to get badge):
  - Product has a published listing with minimum assets (tile image, 250-word description, at least one screenshot/video).
  - Technical verification: integration smoke test passes (see checklist below) against a sandbox tenant within 7 days of submission.
  - Security & privacy: completed the marketplace security questionnaire and confirmation of data flow (hosted vs private).
  - Commercial: agreed standard revenue share or reseller contract on file OR documented exemption approved by legal.
- Fast-path exceptions (for early beta partners): can grant a temporary "beta" badge if: 1) signed confidentiality addendum, 2) launch window <60 days, 3) documented rollout plan with clear SLOs.

Edge-case rule clarifications (examples we've seen):
- Dedicated-only product: If partner only supports Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) and cannot run in Hosted, require an explicit note on the listing tile: "Requires Dedicated capacity; contact sales for provisioning." Badge eligibility still allowed if technical verification runs against a dedicated staging cluster.
- Private (on-prem) offering with no networked smoke test: allow badge if customer reference and completed security review exist; require an additional manual QA sign-off.
- Multi-variant SKU (metered + subscription): treat the listing as a single product for badge purposes if billing mapping is documented (mapping of usage units to SKU ids) and a conversion flow is validated.

2) Pricing bundles: edge cases and recommended rules
- Definitions we use:
  - Base SKU: the primary purchasable unit that appears on the marketplace tile.
  - Add-on SKU: optional extras (e.g., premium support, dedicated capacity add-on).
  - Metered SKU: consumption-based units (tokens, embeddings units).
- Edge case: trial entitlements that convert to Dedicated capacity.
  - Problem: trial typically runs on Hosted sandbox; conversion to Dedicated involves provisioning lead time and a different billing model.
  - Guardrail: trial must include a clear CTA that explains provisioning delay and provide an auto-escalation ticket creation. Copy: "Provisioning Dedicated capacity can take 3–5 business days — a sales rep will help complete setup."
- Edge case: bundle with tiered compute (e.g., small/medium/large instances inside one SKU).
  - Problem: marketplace meters may not represent nested capacity tiers cleanly.
  - Guardrail: expose discrete SKUs per tier (sku-small, sku-medium, sku-large) to avoid proration and reconciliation disputes. If marketplace constraints force single SKU, include a clear pricing table inside the listing and provide a mapping doc in the listing assets.
- Edge case: reseller adds markup + custom terms.
  - Problem: revenue-share math and discounts need to remain auditable.
  - Guardrail: require reseller to publish list price vs effective price internally; legal must sign the reseller pass-through schedule. Badge only allowed if reseller contract is uploaded.

3) Operational & integration checklist (smoke tests + acceptance gates)
- Basic smoke test steps (automated where possible):
  - API call: ping /models endpoint with partner's model id / alias -> verify 200 and model metadata.
  - Generate: basic text generation for short prompt, verify response structure, latency within declared bounds (95th percentile < declared).
  - Billing mapping: create a simulated purchase (sandbox flow) and assert SKU ids recorded in meter events.
  - Trial expiration: trigger trial end and confirm access revocation or conversion flow.
  - RBAC & secrets: validate that marketplace credentials do not leak partner tokens; confirm usage attribution works.
- Non-automated checks:
  - Legal check: reviewed contract for revenue share and indemnities (link to contract vault).
  - Security: completed questionnaire, and if Private, confirm air-gap options documented.
  - Support: runbook for first 30-day incidents.

4) Sample listing copy (tile + short + legal snippet)
- Tile headline (short): "Low-latency LLM inference for product search — Redwood Dedicated ready"
- Short blurb (220 characters): "Fast, predictable LLM inference for search and chat. Choose Hosted for quick trials or Dedicated for production throughput and isolation. Includes built-in caching and quantization options."
- CTA variants: "Start trial (Hosted)" / "Request Dedicated pricing"
- Billing / legal snippet (50–70 words): "Billing is managed via the marketplace. Usage-based items (tokens, embeddings) are metered; Dedicated capacity is billed as a monthly commitment. Contact sales for custom enterprise terms. By purchasing, you agree to partner terms and Redwood's data processing addendum available on our legal page."

5) Risk matrix (quick)
- Risk: Misleading pricing copy -> Severity: High -> Mitigation: Mandatory pricing table asset + legal approval before badge.
- Risk: Trial converts to Dedicated but provisioning fails -> Severity: High -> Mitigation: Auto-escalation + sales SLA + holdback on badge until provisioning runbook exists.
- Risk: Metering mismatch across cloud regions -> Severity: Medium -> Mitigation: Require per-region metering proof and test vectors.
- Risk: Reseller hides fees -> Severity: Medium -> Mitigation: Contractual requirement to disclose effective price and revenue share schedule.

6) Open questions / TODOs
- Should we allow a temporary badge for partner-led private deployments where no sandbox test is possible? (Proposed: yes, for pre-approved customers only.)
- How should we surface provisioning lead times across tiles (single field vs in-copy callout)? (Action: test two variants in RMKT landing experiments.)
- Technical: confirm that billing events for metered tokens propagate through the marketplace ingestion pipeline (RMKT-3421).

Action items (owners):
- Maya: draft the short pricing table template and upload to listing-assets (due 2025-02-24).
- Liam: add dedicated provisioning CTA pattern to the UI component library (due 2025-03-03).
- Diego: confirm contract upload / verification workflow with Legal (due 2025-02-28).
- Sofia: follow up with Platform on automated smoke-test endpoints (RMKT-3421).

Notes to self / scratch:
- Keep badge copy short and consistent with other marketplace badges (avoid product-marketing fluff).
- When in doubt, require a human review — automated gates are helpful but miss nuance for Private/Dedicated setups.

References: link back to the marketplace listing standards Confluence page, previous incidents folder (incidents/marketplace/metering-2024-11) and the RMKT epic in Jira.

End of draft.
